events.title: The First Vatican Council defines papal infallibility
events.shortBlurb: The council solemnly defined the infallibility of the pope in the constitution Pastor Aeternus…
body: The First Vatican Council, convoked by Pius IX and opened in St Peter's on 8 December 1869 with some seven hundred fathers, first issued the constitution Dei Filius on faith and reason on 24 April 1870, then turned to the long-debated schema on the Roman Pontiff. A preliminary vote on 13 July showed 451 for the definition, 62 conditionally for it, and 88 against.

On 18 July 1870, as a thunderstorm broke over St Peter's, the fourth public session approved the constitution Pastor Aeternus by 433 votes to 2, the lone dissentients Bishops Riccio of Cajazzo and Fitzgerald of Little Rock. The constitution defined the pope's primacy of jurisdiction and, under carefully drawn conditions, his infallibility when he defines ex cathedra a doctrine of faith or morals to be held by the whole Church.

Most of the minority had already left Rome, judging the definition inopportune rather than untrue, and all afterward accepted it. The next day France declared war on Prussia; in September Italian troops took Rome at the Porta Pia, and on 20 October 1870 Pius IX suspended the council, its work unfinished, leaving its remaining decrees to a future generation.
